search_queries: targeted PyPI and project-documentation lookups for nine named JSON parsers
uncertainty: Six positive-signal Python JSON third-party paths pass valid nested object and array controls with source-level parser coverage and AFL++ feedback: pydantic 2.14.3 (1,139,429,690 PyPI Stats last-month downloads), orjson 3.13.0 (218,014,317), simplejson 4.3.0 (49,365,386), ijson 3.6.0 (46,615,664), msgspec 0.22.0 (39,138,375), and ujson 6.1.0 (29,543,889). Pydantic embeds Jiter; orjson shares the yyjson C syntax-parser family but this pilot measures its Rust deserializer, not vendored C source lines. ijson uses the asserted yajl2_c backend, with pinned YAJL C tokenizer and Python extension coverage; its source-built embedded YAJL -O0 route differs from the official Linux wheel linkage and optimisation, and its other backends are untested. msgspec uses its own C JSON decoder in _core.c through untyped msgspec.json.decode; its source-built clang -O0 path differs from the official GCC wheel, typed decoding is untested, and JSON decoder sections are counted separately from other codecs in the same file. ujson uses its own UltraJSON C decoder with vendored double-conversion C++ for fractional numbers; both controls equal an exact CPython json oracle tree, and duplicate-key and edge-number behavior is recorded from source, not tested. PyPI package downloads include non-parse uses and transitive installs. Three targeted documented leads remain unverified; bounded PyPI Simple Index search has not yet been run. Python standard json is separately verified.
